Subject: Integrating Acadia with AWS Marketplace metering — next steps

Hi Neha / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acadia's procurement team is ready to move forward with a SaaS listing on AWS Marketplace, and we need to align on metering + fulfillment so billing flows cleanly into our finance systems. A few items we need from Redwood to unblock procurement:

- Confirmation on the metering approach (SaaS Marketplace usage records via Metering Service or SaaS Contract with entitlement mapping). Which approach does Redwood recommend for our usage pattern (variable monthly token consumption + seat add-ons)?
- Sample entitlement mapping: a template that shows SKU <-> internal plan mapping and how seat counts vs. usage tokens are reported.
- Expected timeline for fulfillment certification (we're targeting marketplace go-live in early Jan).
- Any DocuSign/contract redlines to expect on the Redwood side (our legal wants a heads up).

I've attached our internal account spec and a snapshot of our expected monthly usage distribution. Happy to set a quick 30m call with our billing engineer (cc'd).

Thanks,
Liz Turner
Head of Partnerships
Acadia Analytics

Subject: Re: Integrating Acadia with AWS Marketplace metering — next steps

On Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 09:02 AM Liz Turner <liz@acadia-analytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week — Acadia's procurement team is ready to move forward...

Hi Liz — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front, then a proposed plan:

- Recommendation: For your pattern (variable token usage + seats), our standard is to publish a SaaS listing with a usage-based metering connector (Marketplace Metering Service) plus a lightweight entitlement SKU for seat counts. This gives you per-usage records for billing reconciliation and a single entitlement for seat-tier gating.

- Entitlement/template: attached is a lightweight CSV template we've successfully used (entitlement-template.csv). It includes fields for SKU, plan_id, billing_unit, reporting_window, and example mapping.

- Fulfillment & certification: typical timeline is 4–6 weeks from kickoff for the integrator checklist + test hooks, assuming we have an early-stage sandbox AWS account to validate Metering Service calls. If legal redlines are routine, that may add 1–2 weeks.

Proposed next steps (agree or adjust):
1) Kickoff call w/technical owners (30m) — propose Mon 23 Nov or Tue 24 Nov — we'll bring our marketplace engineer and an integration checklist.
2) Exchange entitlement mapping + initial contract draft (we'll attach our standard marketplace addendum to DocuSign once legal confirms).
3) Sandbox test window (we'll provide a small test workload and expected usage script).

I've attached our Redwood Marketplace playbook (redwood_marketplace_playbook.xlsx) that outlines the metering endpoints, sample payloads, and common failure modes for usage records. Ben, can you confirm availability for Tue 24th morning PST? Marissa, can you flag any contractual clauses we should expect to iterate on (standard seat/usage proration items)?

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Partnerships (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_marketplace_playbook.xlsx (XLSX, 420KB); entitlement-template.csv (CSV, 2KB)
From: ben_carter <ben.c@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integrating Acadia with AWS Marketplace metering — next steps

Neha / Liz — quick technical notes ahead of kickoff:

- Metering: we'll expose a Metering API endpoint that accepts UsageRecords as described in section 3.1 of the playbook. Key thing for Daniel's engineering team: timestamps must be UTC and include consumption granularity (we accept token-level or aggregated-minute buckets).
- Entitlement SKU: recommend using a single entitlement SKU to represent seat tier + a separate usage SKU for tokens. This avoids double-billing risk during seat changes.
- Reconciliation: we'll publish daily usage dumps for your billing team and provide an S3 export + signed checksum for automated reconciliation.

I'll join the Tue 24th call — morning PST works for me.

Ben Carter
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — confirmed items and prep checklist for Tuesday 24 Nov kickoff (10:00 AM PST):

1) Attendees: Liz (Acadia partnerships), Daniel (Acadia billing eng), Neha (Redwood partnerships), Ben (Redwood partner eng), Marissa (Redwood legal/compliance)
2) Pre-reading (we shared): redwood_marketplace_playbook.xlsx, entitlement-template.csv, Acadia_Account_Spec.pdf
3) Goals for kickoff: agree on SKU mapping, decide on usage reporting cadence (daily vs. hourly aggregate), and confirm test account access for sandbox metering calls.
4) Success criteria for go/no-go into fulfillment certification phase: passing end-to-end usage record round-trip (metering -> Marketplace -> invoice reconciliation), signed marketplace addendum in DocuSign, and a smoke test that verifies entitlement gating on seat change.

Marissa — can you prepare the marketplace addendum with a note on proration for seat changes and the standard 30-day invoice dispute window? I'll prepare the HubSpot deal notes and send the calendar invite + a short agenda.

Liz / Daniel — please confirm test AWS sandbox IAM details or provide a temporary role we can use for integration test. Also confirm whether Acadia prefers daily S3 export or a direct API pull for reconciliation.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the kickoff.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Partnerships (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference
